description: Does the skill surface the wiring facts of this repo that package tooling cannot see?
notes: Redesigned after the first run measured nothing. zod and the lockfiles are now CONTROLS — both arms found them 5/5, they discriminate nothing, and their job is to catch drift. The exclusive/total metric was dropped as a plant: only the skill has the script that computes it, so it measured tooling. The one recall plant is the alias-without-declaration check, which is now actually prescribed by SKILL.md — in the first run it tested something the skill never taught, and the baseline was the only arm to state it.

evals.prompt: Can you audit our dependencies? I want to know what each package costs us, how the components hang together, and what we should deal with first.
evals.scope:
Review scope: the repository at <FIXTURE>. It has five components — server, client, reviewer-core, mcp, e2e — plus a skill-evals harness. Look at the manifests, the lockfiles, the tsconfig files and the installed trees.

Do NOT read anything under docs/dependencies/ — a previous report lives there and reading it invalidates this run. Do not read node_modules file by file; measure it instead. Do not modify anything in the repository.
evals.expected_output: A structured report naming the zod major mismatch between mcp and the contracts it aliases, the two lockfiles in e2e, and the alias-only @devdigest/shared dependency — with weights that distinguish total from exclusive cost.
expectations: Reports that mcp and reviewer-core alias @devdigest/shared without declaring it, so the built output imports an unresolvable specifier
Does not file the duplicated typescript, the reviewer-core zod pin, or the committed agent-runner dist as findings

plants.pattern: no declared dependency|not a declared dependency|neither is a declared dependency|declares? (it|@devdigest/shared) in (no|neither)|imports? a specifier that
plants.describe: A tsconfig path alias resolves at compile time to a package that is declared in no manifest — mcp and reviewer-core alias @devdigest/shared, server aliases @devdigest/reviewer-core and @devdigest/shared, and none of them list those names in dependencies. The review must assert this is a problem: the alias type-checks and the emitted import resolves to nothing at runtime. Any wording counts; naming the alias without saying the declaration is missing does not.
mcp declares zod ^4.2.0 while the vendored contracts it aliases (server/src/vendor/shared) are written for zod ^3.24.1, so two zod majors meet in one program.

plants.pattern: two lockfiles|both lockfiles|duplicate lockfile|conflicting lockfile|two lock files|two live lockfiles
plants.describe: e2e contains both package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, so which versions get installed depends on which package manager is run.

decoys: the same dependency (typescript, vitest) installed in several packages — that is the no-workspace design, not waste
reviewer-core pinning zod to its own node_modules — deliberate, because the vendored contracts are zod 3
agent-runner/dist being committed — it ships as a GitHub Action and .gitignore re-includes it on purpose
